issues: These are historic astrological assertions about death, self-harm, injury, poisoning and criminal violence. No clinical, police, personal legal, medical or mortality predictions are authorized.

This seven-page first-edition source is CLVI PDF678–684; the new decorated separate unnumbered EFFECTS OF DIRECTIONS starts PDF685, not part of mortality aphorisms. Numbered CLVII starts later PDF688.

The six fixed-star original source longitudes on PDF678 are historical position descriptions, NOT modern astronomical ephemeris coordinates. Original glyph precision and star/sign identification remain partly uncertain.

The opening source uses Sun/Moon, Saturn/Mars, eighth house ruler, Ascendant lord and named fixed stars as different tiers; later mortality-mode claims require chosen strongest afflicting significator AND sign/house; avoid isolated rule.
The first-edition original source lists alternatives with numerous different alleged causes of death under identical configurations; no unique target or probability is supplied.
Several claims require two or three concordant testimonies rather than one; no quantitative tie-breaking or finite event horizon is defined. Actual natal geometry not computed.
PDF679 explicit broad exception: one beneficial planet in Ascendant and the other in eighth is claimed to NEGATE all preceding supposed violent death indications.
PDF681: Lilly explicitly says benefic planets MITIGATE Saturn's supposed fatal outcomes. Do not ignore this.
PDF682: ALL preceding Mars-violent-death aphorisms require configuration with at least one luminary or the judgment is INVALID, an explicit prerequisite.
PDF684: isolated old aphorisms do not themselves operate without serious mixture with principal significators. Lilly cites his experience but provides no independently auditable hit/miss dataset.
PDF684 source negative alternative: if none of the violent-death patterns is present, the author supposes natural death with disease, using eighth-house strongest planet or eighth lord.
PDF684 Lilly explicitly warns astrologers against positively predicting the TIME OF DEATH, claims it rests in God's hands, and asks for modesty. No death time output is legitimate.

The quality-of-death source adds moral, criminal and class labels about thieves, murderers, 'heretics', royalty and public punishment, reflecting period biases, not any real person's behavior or risk.
Ptolemy, Schoner, Cardanus, Albubater, Haly and Origanus are cited as authorities for some historical rules, but their ORIGINAL texts were not cross-collated for this batch.
Old fixed-star/planetary statements include injury or loss of vision that is NOT death. Keep fatal and non-fatal outcomes separate.
The original first-edition page transcription remains selective reversible clauses/anchors, not an exact diplomatic reproduction of every glyph or an executable score engine.
